title: Bound the FrameDecoder buffer + per-frame body (pre-auth memory-exhaustion DoS)
description: Confirmed pre-auth DoS from the 2026-07-02 re-review. FrameDecoder.buffer (FrameDecoder.swift:3) grows unbounded via buffer.append(contentsOf: incoming) (:8); nothing caps buffered bytes or a single declared bodyLength, and the buffer only shrinks once a full frame arrives (:29). A peer that never completes a frame, or declares a huge body below 2^63 (dodging the Int trap in the sibling bead), grows host memory until OOM-kill; with the 16-slot serve cap a few peers suffice. Fix: enforce a max in-flight buffer size AND a max per-frame body length in FrameDecoder; close the connection with a thrown WireError when either is exceeded instead of buffering. Reuse the MAX_FRAME_LENGTH ceiling from the frame-length-reject bead. Acceptance: feeding bytes past the buffer cap, or a body-length past the cap, throws rather than growing unbounded; suite green. Verify: swift test --package-path /Users/tfinklea/git/screenshare --filter FrameDecoder. tier_floor: senior | complexity: S.
close_reason: Explicit maxBufferedBytes backstop (10 + Frame.maxBodyLength) post-drain; per-frame body ceiling landed with 1n6.1. Boundary trickle test pins cap from below; varint-flood test bounds the header stall path. 237/55 green. Commit facc3b8.

title: Reject over-long frame lengths before Int() conversion (pre-auth remote crash fix)
description: Net-new CRITICAL from the 2026-07-02 re-review (decisions.md 2026-07-02). bodyLength is a UInt64 from reader.varUInt() (full 0..2^64-1 range); Int(bodyLength) traps uncatchably on values above Int.max, aborting the whole host process pre-auth (a ~10-byte length prefix reaches the receive loop on any accepted/TOFU connection; processIncoming's do/catch cannot catch a fatal trap). Three sites in FrameDecoder.push(): FrameDecoder.swift:20 (guard compare), :23 (Array slice), :29 (removeFirst). Same shape in Frame.decode at Frame.swift:54 (bodyLength :53) and BinaryReader.data() at BinaryReader.swift:58 (Int(n) from varUInt :57); plus BinaryReader.readBytes at :51 does an offset+count Int addition that overflows near Int.max. Fix: add a MAX_FRAME_LENGTH constant well under Int.max; compare bodyLength in UInt64 space BEFORE any Int() conversion and throw WireError.malformed (existing case, WireError.swift:2) when over the ceiling; change readBytes' guard to count <= storage.count - offset (subtraction, no add overflow). Mirror the skipsUnknownTagWithoutWedging pattern in FrameDecoderTests.swift:38 for a hand-crafted oversized-length frame. No ceiling constant exists in Sources today. Acceptance: a frame declaring a varint length above Int.max, and one just over MAX_FRAME_LENGTH, both throw WireError.malformed with no trap; suite stays green. Verify: swift test --package-path /Users/tfinklea/git/screenshare --filter FrameDecoder (add FrameTests + BinaryCodecTests coverage for the Frame.decode and BinaryReader.data surfaces). tier_floor: senior | complexity: S.
close_reason: Guards at all 3 surfaces (FrameDecoder.push, Frame.decode, BinaryReader.data) compare in UInt64 space vs new Frame.maxBodyLength=16MiB before Int(); readBytes bounds check rewritten subtraction-form. TDD, 4 traps reproduced RED. 235/55 green. Commit 7c5042e.

title: Client file receive dropped the host's size caps (a paired host can fill the iPhone disk)
description: Confirmed (2026-07-02). apps/PortviewClient/Sources/IncomingFileTransfers.swift: chunk() (:40) writes every FileChunk straight to disk (:42) with NO byte accumulator and NO cap; offer() (:28) receives FileOffer (which carries offer.size: UInt64) but never reads it; the private Transfer struct (:16-20) has no received counter. So a paired host can stream unbounded bytes and fill the phone disk. Mirror the HOST cap in Sources/PortviewHostCore/FileReceiver.swift: defaultMaxFileSize 2 GiB (:9) + defaultMaxSessionSize 8 GiB (:12), a per-transfer var received (:14-18) + a receiver-level sessionTotal (:23), enforcement in chunk() at :52 (transfer.received + incoming above maxFileSize OR sessionTotal + incoming above maxSessionSize -> dropTransfer), and dropTransfer (:70-75) closes the handle + removeItem the partial file. Do NOT trust offer.size - count ACTUAL bytes written (the host comment at :7-8 makes this explicit). safeFilename (:58) is the only client-side defense today. Acceptance: a transfer exceeding the per-file or per-session cap is dropped and its partial file deleted, mirroring the host. Verify: swift test on the client target (xcodebuild) with a cap test. tier_floor: senior | complexity: S.

title: EPIC: Host trust model - mutual client auth + revocable pairing (M6 device keypairs)
description: The host authenticates NO client: QUICParameters.server sets only a local identity (no client-verify block), and serveSession grants full keyboard/mouse/clipboard/file control to any peer that completes a bare ClientHello - the pin is a client-side host-verification secret only, never required of the client, and the SAS pairing window is consulted only on the preamble path, never on the streaming path. Cert pinning is one-directional; ClientHello.deviceID is an unauthenticated string. On the intended trusted overlay VPN (Tailscale/WireGuard/home LAN) exposure is bounded to your own devices, but on any shared/untrusted LAN a single hostile device owns the Mac. This epic builds the unbuilt M6 'device keypairs + revocable PairingStore' as the host-side trust anchor, plus the cheap host-side defense-in-depth fixes. Per decisions.md 2026-07-01 arch review (security lens). Threat model per user: local LAN / Tailscale / WireGuard -> P1 (not drop-everything P0), but a real exposure on untrusted LAN.

title: EPIC: QUIC lane-splitting phase 1 (video/audio/stats lane streams off primary)
description: Head-of-line isolation for input vs video. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-01-quic-lane-splitting.md (design-reviewed 2026-07-02, five load-bearing corrections folded — read it before any child). Problem (verified): PortviewConnection is ONE bidi QUIC stream — a lost UDP packet carrying video stalls every message behind it (wire HOL, real on Tailscale/WAN), and send serializes whole frames so a multi-hundred-KB VideoFrame delays a PointerMove even with zero loss (sender HOL). Chosen design: NWConnectionGroup (NWMultiplexGroup) — real QUIC streams on ONE tunnel, one handshake, one pinning evaluation, shared congestion control. Topology: 4 long-lived CLIENT-opened BIDI streams (client-opened uni streams cannot carry host->client payload): primary (unchanged: handshake/control/input/cursor/clipboard/SAS/ping/files) + video + audio + stats. Secondary-stream preamble = [uint8 laneRawValue][32B sessionToken]; token is HOST-minted, delivered via an append-only version-gated ServerHello field (NOT StartSession — that message is client->host and a client-minted token could collide another session). First-byte classifier: <= 6 -> lane preamble; else existing frame path (primary first byte = varint bodyLength >= 6, golden 16; SAS = 33) — a naive unknown-lane-close would break every old client and all pairing. Per-tunnel stream cap (today 100 bidi / 1000 uni in QUICParameters.swift is an amplification surface). Lane death -> fall back to primary ONCE + MUST force an encoder keyframe (HEVC deltas referencing lost frames = frozen video forever). GATED on screenshare-vs9 (latency baseline proves the win measurable); screenshare-350 (negotiated version) already landed. Phase 2 (per-frame streams) = screenshare-10p, gated on the lane-verify A/B. Children: lane-spike, lane-proto -> lane-transport -> lane-host + lane-client -> lane-verify (human).

title: rewake-client: silent-push plumbing + subscription bootstrap + background handler + tap-to-resume

Acceptance: iOS build green; decision/persistence plumbing sim-tested; push delivery + entitlements are device-gated (rewake-verify). Verify: make test-ios. tier_floor: senior | complexity: L.

title: EPIC: CloudKit silent-push re-wake (tap-to-resume after backgrounding)
description: Background re-wake rides the user's own iCloud via CloudKit subscriptions (no servers we host; user decision 2026-07-01, decisions.md). Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-01-cloudkit-rewake.md (design-reviewed 2026-07-02, platform must-fixes folded in — read it before any child bead). Problem: the iOS session is foreground-only; backgrounding suspends the app and drops QUIC, and the in-app reconnectLoop only covers foreground drops within its 30s window — after suspend there is no path back. Best-effort by design (iOS silent-push budget); requires same Apple ID on both devices; fail soft when absent. title: Bound the inbound AsyncStream + add video-lane newest-N backpressure
description: Confirmed (2026-07-02, medium). Fix: give the video path a bounded/newest-N policy (mirror CaptureEngine's .bufferingNewest(2)), or split control (lossless) from video (coalesce-to-latest), or only re-arm receive after the yielded batch is consumed so QUIC flow control engages. This is the inbound-backpressure item the QUIC lane-splitting spec references. Acceptance: a stalled consumer no longer grows memory unbounded; video coalesces to latest while control stays lossless. Verify: swift test --package-path /Users/tfinklea/git/screenshare. tier_floor: senior | complexity: M.

title: HostRunner.nextMessage races an iterator copy-out against a still-running next()
description: Confirmed (2026-07-02). nextMessage (Sources/PortviewHostCore/HostRunner.swift:361-379) runs a read Task (await box.iterator.next()) and a timeout Task guarded by a SingleResumeGate. On the timeout branch the sleep Task wins the gate and resumes nil, but AsyncStream.next() is not cancellation-aware so the read Task is still in flight; line 377 then does iterator = box.iterator, copying the box's iterator back into the caller's inout WHILE the background read may still be mutating box.iterator. MessageIteratorBox is @unchecked Sendable (:349-352) asserting single-task access, which the timeout path violates; SingleResumeGate (:383-390) guards only the continuation, not the iterator. Call site: serveSession peek await nextMessage(from:&inbound, deadline:.seconds(5)) (:428). Fix: do not copy the iterator back until the read actually settles (resolve via the gate to know which task completed, or drive the deadline without an unsynchronized copy-out). Acceptance: no read-after-timeout iterator race; a deterministic test of the timeout path. Verify: swift test --package-path /Users/tfinklea/git/screenshare. tier_floor: senior | complexity: M.

The normal post-stream exit (:487), the catch/error path (:499), and reconnectLoop's exit (:667) all unbind with NO preceding close(); only the explicit user disconnect() closes first (:265-266), and the SAS preamble uses a separate sasConnection. So every non-user-initiated end drops the PortviewConnection without cancelling it, relying on ARC/peer-finish instead of explicit teardown (PortviewConnection.close() = connection.cancel() + inboundContinuation.finish(), PortholeConnection.swift:82-85). title: Add a connect timeout: NWConnection .waiting never resumes awaitReady
description: Confirmed (2026-07-02 re-review). A host that stays .waiting (no route/unreachable) hangs the continuation indefinitely, wedging connect and defeating the 30s reconnect window. The design uses cancellation-as-timeout: awaitReady is wrapped in withTaskCancellationHandler onCancel:{ connection.cancel() } (:93,112-114), so a caller can impose a deadline by cancelling its Task, but no caller does. Caller: connect() awaits awaitReady before startReceiveLoop (:62-69). Fix: impose a bounded connect deadline (a Task.sleep race that cancels the connection, mirroring the host x-deadline pattern) or resume-throw on sustained .waiting. Acceptance: a connect to an unreachable endpoint fails within a bounded time instead of hanging.
